analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen27-tp-decode-loop.md) and additions to docs/architecture/inference.md (around head lines 5094-5157). No executable source was supplied, so the behavior these docs describe cannot be verified here.

The docs describe three things:
1. The Qwen TP finiteness check moves into the selection's sealed sum. A non-finite logit on either rank now fails both ranks before any token is published. The load agreement string `qwen-tensor-parallel-selection-nonfinite-in-sum-v1` makes a mismatched rank refuse to load. If implemented as described, this improves availability (T-010-class hang avoidance) and fails closed with no plaintext exposure.
2. A once-per-load census log line, `darkbloom-qwen-tp-decode-census-v1`. The docs say it reads only host values (route names, layouts, arithmetic switches). It contains no prompt, key or account data, so there is no A-001 or A-003 exposure. The integration pass should confirm the log line carries no request-derived content and is not sent to the coordinator.
3. A rows-check tool (`darkbloom-cluster-tp-check qwen-rows`). It uses random weights over a loopback ring and, per the docs, `qwen-rows run` can also load a registered checkpoint directory directly, reading files without the product's verified load (`QwenTensorParallelVerifiedLoad`: no artifact hashes, no inventory). This is a developer/CI check tool and is explicitly documented as not the product load path. The one thing to confirm is that this tool cannot be reached from the production provider or its launchd service. The changed ranges cover no code, so no weight-substitution (T-012/T-027) regression is evidenced.

No trust boundary, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The remaining uncertainty is that the described Swift implementation (QwenTensorParallelBatchSession, QwenTensorParallelNativeBatchExecutor, QwenRowsCheck) is outside this batch. Another batch should check that the sealed-sum change keeps failure symmetric across ranks and that the census logging leaks nothing.
